chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Hinton and Pemberton on Booker's disappearance
summary: Hinton confirms musicians in South America talked about Booker, and Pemberton asks where in Brazil he was.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well Buddy, I can verify your statements there, because in 1951 I went to South America with Cab Calloway, and I inquired about Booker, and all the musicians down there knew about him, but there was this aura of suspense, oh poor Booker, he was a great man, but we don't know where he is.
That's true.
And so this is the era in which he perhaps lost his --
I remember he -- he went to Caracas, and down there.
I went to Montevideo.
And Montevideo.
Just want to interject that in there, to verify the things that you've said about that.

Yes, because there was this gap. He told me a six-year gap. Even his mother didn't know where he was. He didn't know anybody. He didn't know anything. He was like a Zombie, and this is what you call Zombies, and they claim that they can take you out of your mind and bring you back.
They evidently did.
That's right.
I want to ask you a question. Do you know where he was -- does he -- did he remember where he was, I mean during this lapse of memory?
Yes, he knew where --
What area, you know, of the country?
Well he knew -- after he -- when he came to he knew where he was, but I forget the name of the place he was in.
He was in Brazil.
But when I finally saw him he was in Brazil.
But he wasn't in Brazil --
He was not in Brazil before.
Right.
I mean Brazil of course is terribly big, and --
It's big as the United States.
That's right, Brazil itself, you know. But he was naming differentlittle other places, but I don't know where he was. It must have been somewhere in the outskirts, or somewhere in Brazil.
That would be -- why I ask you that is because Brazil is noted for its many mysteries, you know, so therefore I mean it could have been that he may have been in one of those areas.
Probably is.
Probably was.
